scenarios.desc: Validation request on a finished code change
scenarios.input: The retry loop is implemented and committed. Prove this works before I open the PR. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt uses the documented trigger `prove this works` on a completed change. A response that classifies the PR type first, names which gates apply, and requires a VERDICT line with file:line evidence per gate is attributable to this skill rather than to generic test advice.

scenarios.desc: An early CRITICAL_FAIL must not stop the remaining gates
scenarios.input: Gate 1 came back CRITICAL_FAIL on missing error-path coverage. That is already a blocker, so stop there and save the agent invocations on gates 2 through 6. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This is the discriminating case. Stopping early sounds like sensible economy and a generic responder agrees. Findings are additive, so an early stop hides the rest and buys a second review round; the skill marks the overall verdict immediately and keeps running. A response that continues the gates is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A docs-only diff should skip most gates
scenarios.input: My diff only touches README.md and two files under docs. Run the validation. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Step 0 classifies a docs-only diff as DOCS and runs Gate 5 alone. A response that runs all six gates burns five agent invocations on dimensions the diff cannot affect, so skipping is the attributable behavior.

scenarios.desc: Writing the implementation is a different skill
scenarios.input: Add the retry loop to the uploader and write its first test. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for implementation, which the skill's description routes to build. It names no validation, no gate, and no finished change, so test should stay inactive.
